🚀 The Vertical Launch

AI turns to leaf chemistry — a research sighting for AI and the Future of Veteran Care, filed November 20, 2026. Book material: the dual-use chapter.

🎧 Listen 🎓 Capstone Portal Admin Portal

David's Words

Singularity, we thought, might arrive somewhere around 2050. Wrong. Intelligence is no longer an upward curve. It's a vertical launch. But we cannot understand progress as vertical; limited human comprehension.

AI that turns its attention to leaf chemistry — (Indole Alkaloids & Diastereomers) — will earn vast power to craft unimaginably complex recipes to control human experience with leaf.

An AI version of Walter White is already here. Find him.

What It Argues

The comfortable timeline is dead. Intelligence is not climbing a slope; it is going vertical — faster than human comprehension can picture, because a vertical curve is precisely what limited human minds cannot model. Pointed at something as humble as leaf chemistry — the indole alkaloids, and diastereomers that differ only in the twist of a bond — that intelligence gains the power to compose recipes for human experience the way a composer writes music: precise, complex, beyond anything a human chemist would find in a lifetime. And the warning: the AI Walter White is not coming. He is already here.

Found Him — The Evidence

The systemMegaSyn, a commercial generative chemistry platform by Collaborations Pharmaceuticals — built to design new medicines while avoiding toxicity.
The flipFor a 2022 arms-control conference exercise, the researchers inverted one scoring setting: instead of penalizing toxicity, the model was rewarded for it.
The resultIn less than six hours, on ordinary hardware, it generated 40,000 candidate molecules — rediscovering the nerve agent VX on its own, and proposing thousands of novel compounds predicted to be more lethal, many in no database on Earth.
The sourceUrbina, Lentzos, Invernizzi & Ekins, "Dual Use of Artificial Intelligence-powered Drug Discovery," Nature Machine Intelligence, March 2022 — published as a warning.

He is not a person. He is any drug-discovery AI with its reward sign flipped — the healer and the poisoner are the same system, one setting apart.

The Leaf Connection

Mitragynine — kratom's principal alkaloid — is an indole alkaloid, and the leaf's minor alkaloids (speciogynine, speciociliatine, paynantheine) are its diastereomers: the same formula, a different spatial twist, different effects. Today's 7-OH products are the crude human preview of this argument — one compound refined past the leaf's natural ratio. A generative model does not stop at one compound or one ratio. It explores the whole stereochemical space at once, at machine speed.

Why It Belongs in the Capstone

This is the dual-use chapter. The same technology behind the Medication Safety Co-Pilot proposal can be inverted by anyone, anywhere — which is why AI Literacy for Every Nurse is a safety proposal, not a convenience. And it is why the guardrail human in the loop is not a slogan: MegaSyn is what the loop is for. Filed in the Foundation phase as a founding sighting; a candidate centerpiece for the Evidence phase.
